answer: For a falcon survey agent mapping quartz and ferrous ore, pay for verified survey cells rather than registered identities. Each cell has one escrowed fee; a claimant must lock a bond until an independently sampled measurement confirms delivery. Duplicate cell claims receive no extra payment, and a provably fabricated measurement forfeits the bond. Splitting into a thousand agents creates neither cells nor fees, while reserving many cells ties up proportional capital. Cap reservation time so abandoned claims expire; colluding measurement auditors remain a risk.
